claims.text: The material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature accelerates the alloy's coupled degradation.
A metastable solid-solution phase forms in association with the coupled exposure.
The metastable solid solution undergoes amplitude-modulated decomposition.
Amplitude-modulated decomposition produces a two-phase mixed structure.
The decomposition and resulting mixed structure increase lattice distortion.
The decomposition and lattice distortion reduce corrosion resistance.
Reduced corrosion resistance contributes to accelerated coupled degradation.
The proposed mechanism applies over 500-800 degrees Celsius.
The relevant wear-rate range is 10-50 mm3/m.
The relevant corrosion-rate range is 0.1-1 mm/yr.
A single-phase high-entropy alloy without wear-corrosion exposure is the baseline.
The controlled experiment compares a multi-phase eutectic alloy with a single-phase alloy while exposing both to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature.
Microhardness, wear rate, corrosion rate, and microstructure are measurable responses for the comparison.
Failure of the multi-phase eutectic alloy to show greater coupled degradation than the single-phase alloy would falsify the hypothesis.
The exact amplitude-modulated decomposition mechanism and its effect on corrosion resistance are not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The baseline field defines the single-phase comparator as not exposed to wear and corrosion, whereas the experimental design states that the single-phase comparator is exposed to simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature.
